independent_tests.execution: Python isolated mode; fake unittest responses only, audit hook rejects sockets/process execution and Thread.start is blocked.

scope_checks: Exactly five literal GET URLs are permitted: the PyTorch cu128 torch HTML index and four fixed PyPI version JSON endpoints. Request validation excludes wheel bodies, source archives, HEAD/Range/guessed metadata URLs, arbitrary links and the previously 403 wheel endpoint.
The Torch wheel URL and declared SHA may be retained as record-only metadata; attempting to pass that URL to the request client fails. No link is followed by the parser.

Direct HTTPS uses fixed headers without Cookie or Authorization, no inherited proxy selection and no redirect-following handler. This is a script transport choice, not a change to user network/proxy/security settings. Any denied access stops; no alternate route is authorized.
Attempts are counted before transport; there is no retry/fallback loop. Non-200 status, unexpected content type/encoding, malformed metadata, cap or deadline failure stops the collection.

The per-connection socket timeout is capped at 10 seconds and applies to connection/request/header/body socket operations. An independent parent waits through 110 seconds, then bounded termination/kill waits up to 120 seconds. OS-level start/suspension/final-write timing is explicitly not claimed hard-real-time.

Response-body bytes are read in bounded chunks. A body reaching 1 MiB is conservatively rejected; total response bodies are capped at 8 MiB, and the five-request/per-response constraint is stricter. Headers/TLS/wire overhead are not called body bytes.
Report errors are finite allowlisted codes. Raw exception messages/classes/reprs are not exported by collect, including secret-bearing unexpected exceptions.

PyPI parser rejects duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity/overflow, non-string Requires-Python/license fields, invalid or boolean wheel sizes, invalid SHA256 values, wrong fixed filenames/version/host and yanked entries.

The handoff now distinguishes nine executed cloud fake tests from live collection, which remains unexecuted. Future real Windows execution belongs to a separately authorized local dialogue using verified interpreter/output paths.
practical_result_limits: May establish the official-index-declared Torch filename/hash and fixed PyPI top-level size/hash/release dependency/license declarations. It does not verify any wheel body.
Torch size, Requires-Dist and license remain UNKNOWN; transitive versions/hashes/bytes/licenses, markers/extras, wheel-specific metadata and total download size remain unresolved.

install_ready stays false, and success is explicitly named top_level_metadata_collected_not_install_ready. The artifact is not a lockfile, installer, compatibility certificate or CPU/GPU/model/training approval.

Native Windows supervisor start/termination/persistence behavior was not run here. worker_exit_confirmed is required before treating child exit as confirmed; missing/incomplete reports remain failures.
resolved_findings: Replaced raw exception export with finite codes and verified secret-bearing exceptions are never stringified or echoed.
Added strict nullable-text JSON schema checks, duplicate/nonfinite rejection and fake deadline advancement through transport/header/body phases.
Updated unexecuted-test wording to the actual nine fake-test pass while preserving unexecuted live collection status.
actions_not_taken: No external requests, denied-route retry, wheel/model download, package installation, user-PC access, native worker launch, CUDA, inference, training or publication.
